sections.title: When a custom palette matters more than a season name
sections.html:
Eugene has an option for people who want personal fabric references instead of another four-season label. That changes what you should ask during an inquiry. The relevant comparison is the materials, explanation and follow-up you receive—not whether the consultant uses the same season terminology as an app.

Bernie Burson, Personal Color Designer

Bernie Burson describes an individually designed fabric palette built around the client’s coloring rather than a preprinted seasonal palette. The provider’s professional directory profile identifies Eugene. A current appointment fee was not visible on the reviewed home page.

sections.title: Ask about the physical object you are commissioning
sections.html:
Explain why you are considering a custom palette. Perhaps a standard season contains very few colors you enjoy, or you sew and want to compare real textiles. Ask how the palette is assembled, how many physical samples are supplied, and whether the consultation includes an explanation of useful combinations. Request a written total and the expected appointment length before reserving.

  • What physical samples and written guidance come with the custom palette?
  • How will the session address the clothes or textiles I already use?

sections.title: Use relationships when an exact fabric match is unavailable
sections.html: Try applying the result to a small project first: a shirt and cardigan, a fabric purchase, or a lipstick you wear often. Keep notes about the colors you like in real use. If Stylist AI gives a seasonal direction, treat it as a separate practical reference rather than translating a bespoke palette into an exact season. Different services may answer different styling questions.

sections.title: Seasonal exploration and a bespoke reference can serve different needs
sections.html:
Someone who wants a carefully assembled tactile reference may value the fabric palette more than agreement with a familiar season name. Request examples of the format, how long the process takes and how the explanation is delivered. The reviewed homepage did not provide a current fee, so leave the budget open until you receive a specific quote.

Stylist AI starts from a selfie and a seasonal profile rather than commissioning custom fabric samples. It adds outfit combinations, makeup and hair previews, and camera-based color comparison on your phone. Use it if you want a practical way to explore possibilities first. Choose personal palette design when the physical materials and individual discussion are the part you wish to invest in.

editorial.leadHtml:
A custom palette is a collection to understand, not a list of colors you must buy.

Before commissioning one, ask how the analyst explains the relationship between its samples and the clothes already in your wardrobe.
editorial.ctaTitle: Explore color relationships before collecting more labels
editorial.ctaText: Use Stylist AI to try combinations, then decide whether a bespoke fabric reference would add value.
